learning: If bend progress rises but the robot still leaves the line, combine lead with a modest spread increase at 0.6 kg. If progress does not move, the next lever is sensor_size 0.016 or a larger spread with mass kept at 0.6 kg. If the oval loses finishes, lead is adding lag and y should return toward 0.06.
notes: Baseline drivetrain and controller with the sensor row moved forward to y=0.07 m, isolating look-ahead as the only change from iteration 0. Oval should stay near 20/20 at about 1.65 s, and bend progress should rise above 0.17 and 0.12 if lead is the limit.
rationale: Iteration 0 (baseline: 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius, array at ±0.024 m, sensors at y=0.05) finished the oval 20/20 at 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15. Its s-bend and slalom runs went off track at progress 0.17 and 0.12, with max_error about 0.061 m at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 1 (wider ±0.032 array with 0.10 m track, 0.5 kg, 0.033 m radius) dropped the oval to 17/20 and raised oscillation to 0.26, while the bends gained only partly (0.24, 0.19). Iteration 2 (wide array with baseline drivetrain at 0.5 kg) gave oval 15/20 with oscillation 0.21 and no bend gain beyond iteration 1. The oval losses in iterations 1 and 2 are shared by the 0.5 kg mass and the wide array, so the evidence cannot separate them. Iteration 2 also showed the wider array does not reliably improve the bends. The bend failures persist across all designs, which points toward look-ahead as the untested lever. This iteration returns to the proven 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track and 0.03 m radius drivetrain, keeps the baseline controller (kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction), and moves only the sensor row forward from y=0.05 to y=0.07 m. The ±0.024 m 12 mm-pitch array stays fixed so the oval should be unaffected. I expect the oval to stay near 20/20 and 950, and the s-bend and slalom progress to rise above 0.17 and 0.12. This is untested.
